sections.title: 8. Module Sequencing (Phase 0-5)

claims.text: Phase 0 — Build/toolchain uplift: Kotlin uplift, AGP uplift, Gradle 8, jcenter removal, targetSdk to 34.
Phase 1 — Config/secrets/logging: $API_VERSION resolver, release-logging posture fix, secret rotation / keystore setup.
Phase 2 — DI modernization: Koin 2.2 → Koin 3 or Hilt migration. Decision recorded as ADR.
Phase 3 — Repository / ViewModel uplift: StateFlow over LiveData, coroutine-first repositories, structured concurrency.
Phase 4 — UI migration: XML → Compose screen-by-screen; kotlin-android-extensions removal; DayNight theme preserved.
Phase 5 — Regression + cleanup: Screenshot parity suite, accessibility scanner baseline, golden-feature matrix, dead-code sweep.

sections.narrative: Module sequencing is filtered by runtime reachability — active + dormant modules progress through Phase 0-5; broken modules require an explicit preserve/fix/drop decision; orphaned + test-only modules are excluded by default.

sections.title: 9. Technical Enablement Phase
sections.narrative:
Technical enablement concentrates on removing the constraints captured in §3 before any behaviour change lands. Scope:
- CI/CD pipeline introduction (the non-applicability register   records its current absence).
- Build matrix: API 21, 30, 34 — Firebase Test Lab slots.
- Linter + formatter baseline committed to repo (ktlint + detekt).
- Screenshot-test harness bootstrapped (Paparazzi or Shot).

sections.title: 10. Testing / Equivalence Harness

claims.text: Cold start budget: Cold-start time ≤ 2s on a mid-tier device (Pixel 6a class). — Mobile users abandon apps that take longer than 3s to reach a first interactive frame; 2s leaves headroom for flaky networks. Verification: Run `am start -W` against a signed release build 10× per commit on a Firebase Test Lab mid-tier device; p95 must stay under 2s.

Scroll frame timing: Frame time p99 ≤ 16ms during RecyclerView scroll. — Sub-16ms frames correspond to smooth 60Hz rendering; exceeding it produces visible jank. Verification: FrameMetrics + PerfettoTrace on dashboard + transaction list scroll scenarios.

Image decode memory: Peak memory during profile-picture decode ≤ 50MB. — EXIF-oriented bitmaps can spike memory; exceeding the budget risks OOM on low-end devices. Verification: Android Profiler memory snapshot during the upload workflow; fail if heap grows >50MB over baseline.

Config-change restoration: Every screen restores scroll state + form fields across a rotation without data loss. — Config changes destroy/recreate Activities; unsaved state is a class of defect the v2 app must not inherit. Verification: Espresso tests that rotate the device at each visible screen and assert state equivalence.

Offline UX: Network failure surfaces a readable error state without crashing. — Sandbox / demo users often hit flaky Wi-Fi; a crash on offline undermines parity evidence. Verification: Android UI tests with airplane-mode toggled on every ViewModel-backed screen.

Contrast baseline: All interactive elements meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast on the DayNight theme. — Baseline accessibility is a hard requirement for app-store submission and inclusive UX. Verification: Accessibility Scanner run on every screen; no CRITICAL contrast failures.

Accessible names: Every clickable element has a non-empty contentDescription or text. — TalkBack users cannot navigate unlabelled buttons. Verification: Android Accessibility Test Framework (AATF) rule `CLICKABLE_ITEM_NEEDS_LABEL`.

API level matrix: API 21 → API 34 supported; CI runs instrumentation tests on API 21, API 30, API 34. — Current Sweet Bank targets API 21-30; the migration must at least hold that floor and add API 34 for Play Store compliance. Verification: Firebase Test Lab test matrix covering the three API levels.

Screenshot parity: Golden screenshot per primary screen; CI fails on pixel-diff >1%. — Preserves visual parity during the Compose migration — tests catch subtle Material theme drift. Verification: Shot or Paparazzi test suite, one per Fragment / composable screen.

Release logging posture: HttpLoggingInterceptor level must be NONE on release; BODY only on debug. — The current app logs request bodies at BODY level regardless of build type, exposing bearer tokens in logcat. Verification: Gradle lint rule + build-type conditional in NetworkModule.kt; CI gate reads the generated APK manifest.

Bearer token storage: API bearer must come from a secure source (BuildConfig backed by keystore, EncryptedSharedPreferences, or server-issued token), never hardcoded. — The current `Bearer $API_KEY` default in network module is a credential leak. Verification: Static-analysis rule on AccountApi / PayeesApi; gate fails when a hardcoded bearer is present in source.

facts.text: IO Dispatcher for Repository Work: Network / disk work is hopped off the main thread via Dispatchers.IO to keep the UI responsive.
Empty Collection Fallback: Null / missing collections are defaulted to an empty list so downstream UI code never has to null-check.
LiveData Post-to-Main: Background-thread results are delivered to observers via postValue so the emit lands on the main thread.
